paper_metadata.title: Powder Metallurgical Manufacturing of Ti-Nb alloys Using Coarse Nb Powders

evidence.quote: In this study, manufacturing of (α+β) Ti-Nb alloys by powder metallurgical techniques using coarse HDH Nb (D50 = 110 μm and D 50 = 255 μm) and HDH Ti (D50 = 22.6 μm) powders as starting materials was described.

other.slurry_composition: 80 wt.% metal powders, 18 wt.% isopropanol, 1 wt.% ethylcellulose, 1 wt.% PEG

evidence.quote: For tape casting, alcohol-based slurries were produced by mixing the metal powders (80 wt.%), isopropanol (18 wt.%) and ethycellulose (1 wt.%) and PEG (1 wt.%). ... The Ti16Nb tapes were produced in a manual tape casting line, the position of doctor blade was adjusted to obtain tapes of ca. 800 μm thickness in the green state.
Green tapes were cut in 1 mm x 5 mm pieces and placed in an oven at 60 oC for 60 minutes for solvent evaporation.
Thermal debinding and sintering were performed in a high vacuum furnace. For thermal debinding, the samples were heated up with 1 °C/min to 500 °C held at this temperature for 30 minutes.
Sintering was performed at 900, 1000, 1100 and 1200 °C with dwell time of 180 minutes.

other.feedstock_composition: metal powders mixture with binder system: 70 vol.% paraffin wax, 25 vol.% polyethylene, 5 vol.% stearic acid

evidence.quote: Green parts were produced by warm compaction of MIM feedstocks following the procedures described elsewhere31,32, which basically consist of adding the MIM feedstock to a die of 11 mm diameter – adjusting the amount of feedstock to obtain green parts of ca. 19 mm height - and then compacting the MIM feedstock by applying a uniaxial pressure of 110 MPa, at 150 oC for 120 s.

other.purpose: remove paraffin wax and stearic acid

evidence.quote: After warm compaction, the samples were immersed in n-hexane bath (50 °C, 24 h) to remove paraffin wax and stearic acid.
Thermal debinding and sintering were performed in a high vacuum furnace. The samples were heated up with 1 °C/min to 500 °C held at this temperature for 120 minutes to remove the binder
then sintering was performed at 1200 °C for 180 minutes.
